Oil is near-neutral (transmits only via inflation->rates). Rising remittances swell low-cost deposits and home-remittance fee income (+0.2).

Weaker trade volumes reduce trade-finance flows and macro growth
Import bill widens, reserves/PKR stress, sovereign-linked asset-quality risk

causal_chains.trigger: Government launches/revives a subsidised low-cost housing finance scheme (Mera Pakistan Mera Ghar-type mark-up subsidy)
causal_chains.mechanism: Subsidised mortgage rates unlock latent housing demand, driving construction starts. Cement, rebar/long-steel, glass, wiring/cable and sanitaryware offtake rise; banks book subsidised mortgage assets (govt bears the mark-up differential) growing consumer-loan books; REIT/real-estate values re-rate. Effect is strongest when the policy rate is low so the subsidy gap is affordable for the exchequer.
causal_chains.evidence: 2020-21 SBP Mera Pakistan Mera Ghar low-cost housing scheme with mark-up subsidy drove a cement-demand and construction-package rally; construction was granted amnesty/incentive package (empirical).

causal_chains.trigger: New EV / auto policy with duty concessions on EVs and charging infrastructure and higher tariffs protecting local assembly
causal_chains.mechanism: EV incentives shift demand toward electric drivetrains and lift long-run electricity demand, favouring power generation/distribution and cable/charging infrastructure. Incumbent ICE assemblers face transition capex and margin risk from new (often Chinese) entrants; over time petrol/HSD volume growth for OMCs is capped. Auto-parts localisation requirements can benefit domestic vendors.
causal_chains.evidence: Pakistan's 2019 National EV Policy targeted EV penetration with duty concessions; new Chinese EV entrants (BYD, MG) intensifying incumbent competition (directional/logic + policy record).

causal_chains.trigger: Pakistan enters a new IMF programme (EFF/EFF-successor) with upfront conditions
causal_chains.mechanism: IMF conditionality forces PKR to a market-clearing (weaker) level, policy-rate hikes to anchor inflation, fiscal tightening and tariff/subsidy reform. Near term this compresses domestic-cyclical demand (cement, autos, steel, consumer durables) via high rates and squeezed disposable income; banks benefit from higher rates and re-priced sovereign books; USD-earning exporters and E&Ps/IPPs gain from depreciation. Crucially, programme approval de-risks the sovereign, unlocks bilateral/multilateral inflows and typically triggers a broad market re-rating once stability is priced.
causal_chains.evidence: 2023 IMF SBA and 2024 EFF: PKR devaluation, policy rate to 22%, followed by a strong KSE-100 re-rating as default risk receded (empirical).

causal_chains.trigger: Strait of Hormuz closure / geopolitical oil-supply shock spiking Brent sharply
causal_chains.mechanism: Higher crude directly boosts E&P realisations and refinery GRMs/inventory gains, and OMCs book inventory gains. But the wider import bill widens, pressuring PKR and reserves; furnace-oil power cost and circular debt worsen; energy-intensive and import-dependent cyclicals (cement, autos, glass, chemicals) face cost-push and demand destruction; inflation forces rates higher, hurting rate-sensitive sectors.
causal_chains.evidence: Pakistan imports the bulk of its oil needs and is a net energy importer; oil spikes historically widen the current-account deficit and pressure PKR (structural/logic; ~15-20% of imports are petroleum group).

causal_chains.trigger: Major cotton crop failure (floods/pest) cutting the domestic cotton harvest
causal_chains.mechanism: A short local crop forces higher raw-cotton imports at a time of firm global prices and a weak PKR, sharply raising the dominant input cost for spinners and composites and squeezing margins. Value-added composites with pricing power and forward cover fare relatively better than pure spinners; fertiliser/agri-input demand is disrupted for the season.
causal_chains.evidence: 2022 floods slashed the cotton crop, forcing large cotton imports and compressing spinning margins (empirical).

causal_chains.trigger: OGRA/government raises natural-gas (feedstock and captive) tariffs
causal_chains.mechanism: Higher feedstock gas raises urea production cost for fertiliser producers (margin hit unless fully passed through to farmers), while higher captive/RLNG tariffs raise energy cost for textiles, glass and other gas-intensive industry, eroding export competitiveness and margins. Fertiliser demand can also soften if urea prices are raised to protect margins.
causal_chains.evidence: Repeated gas tariff/GIDC and feedstock-price hikes (2019-2023) pressured fertiliser margins and captive-power textile costs (empirical/policy record).

causal_chains.trigger: Government imposes a super-tax / one-off windfall levy on high-earning sectors
causal_chains.mechanism: A retrospective super-tax (e.g. up to 10%) directly cuts post-tax earnings and payout capacity for the most profitable, well-capitalised sectors — banks, fertiliser, E&Ps and large-cap cement — compressing EPS and dividend yields and de-rating those names, with knock-on drag on the index given their weight.
causal_chains.evidence: FY2022 budget's 10% super-tax on large sectors and elevated bank ADR-linked taxation cut sector earnings and triggered de-rating (empirical).

causal_chains.trigger: CPEC phase-2 / renewed Chinese financing for infrastructure, SEZs and power projects
causal_chains.mechanism: Fresh Chinese-financed infrastructure, industrial-zone and power build-out lifts structural demand for cement, long/flat steel, power equipment and cabling, and improves construction-cycle visibility. Coal-IPP and transmission projects support power names; sustained project pipeline supports cement/steel utilisation.
causal_chains.evidence: CPEC phase-1 (2015-2020) drove a cement/steel capacity and demand upcycle; phase-2 SEZ/industrial focus (directional, based on prior CPEC impact).

causal_chains.trigger: SBP begins a policy-rate cutting cycle as inflation decelerates
causal_chains.mechanism: Falling rates revive auto financing and construction demand, cut financing cost for levered cyclicals, and lift discounted valuations of high-payout and long-duration assets (REIT, cement). Banks face NIM compression on the asset-sensitive book, partly offset by improving asset quality, credit growth and capital gains on their bond portfolios.
causal_chains.evidence: 2024-25 SBP easing cycle (policy rate cut from 22% toward low-teens) drove a cyclicals and broad-market rally (empirical).

causal_chains.mechanism: A large rupee slide instantly boosts PKR earnings of USD exporters (textiles, IT) and USD-linked E&Ps and IPPs, but raises input costs and squeezes importers — auto assemblers (CKD), pharma (APIs), chemicals (feedstock), vanaspati (palm oil) and food. It also stokes inflation, pulling forward rate hikes.
causal_chains.evidence: 2022-23 PKR slide from ~175 to ~300/USD lifted IT/textile exporter earnings while crushing auto volumes and pharma margins (empirical).

causal_chains.trigger: Global cotton price spike (ICE/NY futures surge)
causal_chains.mechanism: Higher international cotton lifts the primary input cost for spinners and composites. Pure spinners with limited pricing power are hit hardest; integrated value-added exporters can pass some cost through and may gain if selling prices reset upward. Substitution demand pushes toward polyester fibre.
causal_chains.evidence: 2021-22 global cotton rally to multi-year highs compressed Pakistani spinning margins and boosted PSF substitution demand (empirical).

causal_chains.trigger: Government resolves/reduces power-sector circular debt via a bond issuance or tariff/settlement package
causal_chains.mechanism: Clearing stranded receivables improves cash flows and reduces working-capital financing for IPPs, OMCs and E&Ps (whose gas/oil dues sit at the top of the chain). It de-risks dividends for HUBC/KAPCO-type names and improves PSO/SNGP/SSGC liquidity, supporting a re-rating across the energy chain.
causal_chains.evidence: Periodic circular-debt payment/PIB-issuance settlements (2013, 2020-21) improved energy-chain liquidity and payouts (empirical).

causal_chains.trigger: US Fed rate-cut cycle plus frontier/EM inflows and improved Pakistan external position
causal_chains.mechanism: Lower US rates and risk-on flows favour high-beta frontier markets; combined with a stable PKR and reserves, foreign and leveraged local flows return to PSX. High-beta and index-heavy sectors — banks, E&Ps, cement — and brokerage/securities firms benefit most from rising turnover and re-rating.
causal_chains.evidence: Historically PSX turnover and foreign flows correlate with global risk appetite and Fed cycle; MSCI FM inclusion episodes lifted turnover (directional/logic + prior flow behaviour).

causal_chains.trigger: Government grants sugar export permission alongside a higher cane support price
causal_chains.mechanism: Export permission clears domestic surplus and lets mills realise firm world prices in USD, while a higher support price raises cane cost but is typically more than offset by better sugar and molasses/ethanol realisations; bagasse cogeneration adds a secondary earnings leg.
causal_chains.evidence: Periodic sugar export approvals during surplus years improved mill realisations; support-price hikes raise input cost for downstream food users (empirical/policy record).
